title: Call digest, version 2
description:
One completed call's quality checks, at call level and per client session, with the evidence needed to inspect each outcome.

Stored at `digests/calls/{callId}.json`. `callId` alone is the key because it is a UUID and therefore globally unique; `roomId` is carried inside because the dashboard's route is /{roomId}/{callId} and a reader holding only a digest must still be able to link back.

This one file serves both pages. The call page reads `checks` and `coverage`; a client page reads its own entry in `clients`. The roll-up in `checks` is computed from `clients[].checks` in the same pass, so the two cannot disagree — which is the whole reason there is no separate client digest.

What is NOT here: no metric warehouse, no histograms, no scores. A check answers a question and points at the evidence; anything a reader wants beyond that is in the raw samples, which stay available.

checks.title: Call-level roll-up, one entry per catalogue check
checks.description: Counts of how the client sessions answered. Deliberately counts and not a verdict: a call where one of eight clients froze is not simply 'failed', and collapsing it to one word is how a dashboard starts lying.

sfuIds.description: Every SFU that served the call, from the router reports. Context only — a multi-SFU call is still one call.

callCoverage.title: Call-level coverage
callCoverage.description: Spelled out in full rather than composed from common.json#/$defs/coverage with allOf. That composition is the obvious move and it does not work: the shared definition seals itself with additionalProperties:false, so every call-level field added beside it is rejected by the inner schema. Listing the three second-fields twice is the cheaper mistake, and a test pins them against the client-level ones.

clientsObserved.description: Client sessions with at least one sample.

clientsAssessed.description: Of those, the ones where at least one check reached passed or failed. The gap between this and clientsObserved is the honest unknown.

callSummaryPresent.description: Whether call-summary.json was readable. Without it the call's bounds and display names are inferred from samples, which is weaker.

limitations.description: Plain sentences naming what could not be assessed and why. Shown verbatim; the one place prose is stored, because a limitation is specific to one call and cannot be resolved from a registry.

id.description: A key of the shipped check catalogue. The question text, section and order are resolved from there, not stored here.

failedSeconds.description: Assessed client-seconds inside a failing interval. Client duration, not call duration and not stream duration — the three differ and conflating them is how an 8-client call reports more impaired time than it lasted. Absent when the rule has no interval.

clientDigest.title: One client session's checks
clientDigest.description: `clientId` is unique within this call only. The addressable identity of this session is the call's `roomId` and `callId` plus this `clientId`.

classification.title: What this client session's evidence amounts to
classification.description:
Disjoint by construction, and ordered: a session showing a user-experience symptom is `qoe-symptom` even if it also had a transport condition, because the symptom is the thing that happened to the person.

`qos-only` is a transport or connectivity condition with no symptom evidence — worth surfacing, and NOT a claim that anyone noticed. `no-issue-within-coverage` is exactly that and not 'healthy': it is bounded by what could be assessed. `insufficient-evidence` is a session that could not be classified at all.

clientCheck.title: One question, answered for one client session

rule.description: The rule as applied, in one line, with the threshold that was used. Stored per outcome rather than resolved from the catalogue because a rule can be parameterised and the reader needs the value that actually decided this answer.

why.description: Required reading for `not-assessable`: what evidence was missing. 'no remote-inbound RTP report in 1309s of samples' is useful; 'unavailable' is not.

interval.description: When the fault was observed. Absent on a pass, and absent where the rule is not interval-bounded.

issues.description: Built-in issues that evidence this outcome. A failing check normally has at least one; a check with issues but no statistic is still `not-assessable`, because a detector firing is a report, not a measurement.

evidence.description: Where to look. Ordered most-specific first, so the UI's primary link is evidence[0].
